title: Let the PIN service find its HSM after a restart

blocks.text: Your server translates PIN blocks through an HSM driver that is a QBean of its own: it registers itself in the `NameRegistrar` under its name when it starts. `PinService`, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PinService.java`, asks it for every translation. Its descriptor is in the comment at the top of the file.

The service worked in testing, where it was copied into a server that was already running. Since the last restart it has done nothing, and an operator can't tell that from JMX. The HSM team also redeploys their driver now and then, while the server runs.

Finish `awaitHsm` and `hsm`, marked `TODO`. About six lines in total. When you're done, the service works after a restart, an operator can see when it can't work and start it again once the HSM is back, and it follows the HSM driver through a redeploy.
The tests deploy your service and a stand-in HSM driver with a real Q2 in the test's JVM: in the same pass, in different passes, without the HSM, and with the HSM redeployed while the service runs.

cases.says: added to a server whose HSM driver is already running, the PIN service starts and translates through it
deployed in the same pass as the HSM driver, the PIN service still starts, because it looks for the HSM only once starts begin
with no HSM the start fails, so the service is Failed rather than Started, and it can be started again once the HSM is up
after the HSM driver is redeployed, translations go to the new instance, not the stopped one

origin.section: 14.5 Nothing Is Started Until Everything Is Initialised, So a QBean Looks for What It Needs in `startService`

concepts: Within one pass every init comes before every start, so a QBean looks for another in startService, fails the start when it is missing, and looks it up again at each use.
